1|# /build
2|
3|Everything in this directory was written during the Meta Global AI Developer Hackathon, October 26 to November 4, 2026. See [NEW-WORK.md](../NEW-WORK.md) for the ledger.
4|
5|Contents:
6|
7|- `src/provider.ts`: the provider seam. `messagesProvider` for the Meta Model API and Baseten through the Anthropic SDK base-URL swap, `openAiProvider` for OpenAI-compatible hosts. Sends effort, the JSON Schema output contract, and a cache marker; never sends the fields the Meta endpoint rejects. `src/schema.ts` is the appeal contract and validator (every sentence and every piece of evidence carries a verbatim quote from a cited chart entry); `src/cost.ts` the price table.
8|- `src/litmus.ts`: the LITMUS gate, written from the two Zenodo papers. Deterministic, fail-closed, external to the model. Per sentence: resolve the citation, require the quote verbatim in that entry, require every number, date, code, and laterality to be sourced from the entry, the criteria, the denial, or the case facts. Only this module can mint `verified`. v1.4 (Oct 28): a side, left or right, is a hard token wherever it names a side, not only before a fixed anatomy list; found by the mutation harness below.
9|- `src/harness.ts`: runs the 50 cases through a provider and the gate, scores each against the grading key, and writes a results file. `npm run harness -- --provider meta --model muse-spark-1.3` (or `--provider baseten --model meta-models/muse-spark-open-1026`). Concurrency 8, effort low (`--effort medium` or `high` for the sweep of README Table 6, `results/effort/`). `--repair N` (default 0, README 2.9): a blocked warranted draft is sent back to the model with the gate's record verbatim and the revised draft re-gated, never on a declined draft; the result keeps `firstOutcome`, `firstGate`, and `repairs[]`, and the summary a `repair` block (`results/repair/`, Table 5). `--case <id>` (repeatable) picks cases; `--verbose` streams one line per tool call and the verdict to stderr; `--live` is verbose with no results file unless `--out-dir` is given, and `npm run live -- --case case-001` is the primary configuration under it. The two tools that open something, `read_entry` and `policy_status`, require a one-sentence `why`, recorded on the trace event, because the API returns only redacted thinking. `--out-dir results/repeats` writes a run outside the scoreboard's directory: the viewer reads only `results/`, so repeat runs for run-to-run variance live in `results/repeats/` and reach the README only as Table 2's ranges (the build log reads `results/`, `results/repeats/`, and `results/payer/`). `--agentic` switches to the tool-calling path: the model gets a chart index and the tools `list_entries` and `read_entry`, `provider.ts` loops on tool_use, and every case records a `trace[]` of tool calls and `reading` statistics (entries read of chart size, grading-key entries read).
10|- `scripts/regate.ts`: re-run the gate over the drafts stored in a results file (`npm run regate -- --file results/<file>.json`); the gate is pure in its inputs and refuses if the stored inputHash differs. `scripts/advise.ts`: the advisor pass (`npm run advise -- --file results/<file>.json --provider meta --model muse-wonder-1.0`), one structured question per case about whether the cited quotes satisfy each criterion; writes `advice` per case and `summary.advice`, never touches the gate.
11|- `litmus-gate/`: the gate as a tool. `npm run gate -- check draft.json case.json` (exit 0 pass, 1 blocked, 2 declined; `--json` for the full record), `npm run gate -- mcp` serves `litmus_verify_draft`, `litmus_check_sentence`, and `litmus_contract` over stdio (MCP TypeScript SDK v2), `npm run gate:build` bundles one file for the `bin`, `npm run gate:smoke` drives the built server over stdio as a host would. Its [README](litmus-gate/README.md) has the host configuration.
12|- `scripts/mutate.ts`: the mutation harness (`npm run mutate`). It takes every sentence the kept runs verified, injects one fabrication at a time (a number replaced by a value absent from every admissible source, a date shifted, a side swapped, the citation moved to an entry that lacks the quote, a word dropped from the quote; separately, wrong numbers and sides that happen to appear in the criteria, denial, or case facts; separately, a negation flipped or a pronoun swapped) and runs the gate on each, reporting the catch rate per class. Writes `results/mutations/report.json`; the report under gate v1.3, which found 48 swapped sides passing, is kept as `report-v1.3.json`. Tests in `tests/mutate.test.ts`.
13|- `src/chart.ts`: the `policy_status` tool, a live query against CHART's coverage index (pre-existing data source, labeled as such). One metered query per authority for the whole run, since the index returns the same table whatever the code or date; repeats answer from memory and are marked `cached this run` in the trace. `npm run harness -- --provider meta --model muse-spark-1.3 --agentic --chart` with `CHART_API_KEY` in `.env`.
14|- `results/`: one results file per model from the October 27 runs, the three agentic runs of October 28, and the three agentic runs with the live CHART tool (file names carry `-agentic` and `-chart`; each case has its trace and reading statistics). `results/repeats/` holds repeat runs of the live-CHART configurations for run-to-run variance; `results/payer/` holds the three payer-side runs of Table 4; `results/mutations/` holds the mutation harness reports. The post hoc directories of README 2.9 to 2.12: `results/repair/` (one repair turn, Table 5), `results/effort/` (effort medium and high, Table 6), `results/intake/` (the letters read back, Table 7), and `results/dictated/` (the dictation stand-in); the viewer lists the first two last in its picker and keeps them off the scoreboard. Each holds the run settings, the summary (outcomes, gate pass rate, sentences verified, latency percentiles, tokens, cost, stakes defended, citation precision), and every case with its draft and the gate's per-sentence record. The repository README reports the summaries.
15|- `synthetic/`: the 50-case synthetic denial set, generated by `src/synthetic/generate.ts` from the templates in `src/synthetic/templates/` (`npm run synthetic`). See `synthetic/README.md` for the composition, the stakes, and the labels. `synthetic/letters/`: each denial as a one-page remittance letter image, 1275 by 1650 px, deterministic from the case file, rendered by `src/synthetic/letters.ts` through Playwright's Chromium (`npm run letters`; README 2.11) with a manifest of hashes that `tests/letters.test.ts` checks.
16|- `src/intake.ts`: document intake of the letters (`npm run intake`): each image to muse-spark-1.3 as a base64 image block with a JSON schema for eight administrative fields, each scored against the case file; writes `results/intake/` (README Table 7). Nothing clinical is sent or judged.
17|- `src/dictation.ts`: dictation (`npm run dictate -- --audio <wav> --case case-001 --entry note-013`, README 2.12): transcribes a recording with Muse Voice Transcribe through the Meta Model API, writes the transcript as that entry's text into a copy of the case under `synthetic/dictated/`, and runs the primary configuration on it with `--verbose` into `results/dictated/`; the gate's quotes against that entry are quotes of speech. Stops with a clear error naming the file when the recording is not there.
18|- `viewer/`: the judge-facing replay page. `window.ypid.spotlight('chart' | 'criteria' | 'draft' | 'sentence:3' | 'verdict' | 'board' | 'writ' | …)` rings one region and dims the rest while a take is recorded (`viewer/src/spotlight.ts`); the page never sets it on its own, and `null` clears it. `npm run viewer` copies `results/` (and `results/payer/`, `results/repair/`, `results/effort/`, listed last and kept off the scoreboard) and `synthetic/cases/` into `viewer/data/`, bundles `viewer/src/main.ts` to `viewer/app.js`, and typechecks; then serve the directory statically (`npm run viewer:serve`, port 8787). `npm run viewer:check` drives the built page in headless Chromium (`scripts/check-viewer.ts`, playwright-core on Playwright's own Chromium) and fails on any console or page error: the Compare tab for every case, the repair banner and re-stamp on a repaired case, the typed `why`; that the page at 1600 wide renders pixel for pixel the same with every narrow-screen media block stripped from the stylesheet (so the phone shell cannot touch what the recorded takes show); and that on a 390-wide phone viewport the dock is shown, drives the replay to its verdict, opens the writ, opens the footnote sheet from a footnote number and walks it, lands a case opened without a step on the writ, and nothing runs wider than the screen. The published copy is at https://demo.hemeehr.com, built by Vercel from `vercel.json` at the repository root on every push to main. `viewer/src/replay.ts` holds the replay logic as pure functions (timeline, state at a cursor, scoreboard rows) and is tested; `main.ts` only renders.
19|- `tests/`: `npm test`. <!-- test-count:start -->263<!-- test-count:end --> tests (the count is written by `npm run log`), no network except the letters image test, which re-renders two letters in the locally installed Chromium and skips without it; the model transport is stubbed.
20|- `src/smoke.ts`: one synthetic denial through each configured host (`npm run smoke`). `src/probe.ts`: effort, JSON Schema, and prompt-cache probe (`npm run probe`). `src/test-call.ts`: the first call to the Meta Model API (`npm run test-call`). Each reads keys from the repository `.env`: `MODEL_API_KEY`, `BASETEN_API_KEY` for Baseten, and `CHART_API_KEY` (or `CHART_VERIFY_KEY`, `CHART_CUSTOM_TOKEN`) for the `policy_status` tool.
21|
22|Models are called only over hosted APIs; nothing runs locally.
23|
24|All data used here is synthetic. No real patient data is used anywhere in this repository.

# Review: your-procedure-is-denied (build/)

**Verdict.** The core referential idea is sound and unusually well documented: verbatim-quote checking, fail-closed verdicts, and the stored-result tables are real and mostly reproduce exactly. But the gate is not the fabrication-proof check the Abstract and Conclusion claim. I confirmed multiple inputs in the gate's own declared scope — dates, numbers, codes, and anatomical sides — that return `verified`, including one assembled packet that returns `pass`. The mutation study's "5,824 of 5,824 hard corruptions caught" is true only inside the corruption shapes the harness knows how to generate; the bypasses below are outside those shapes and outside [the gate tests](</tmp/claude-1000/-home-james-projects-your-procedure-is-denied-build/9fc98b9d-e5c7-45fe-9c8e-9ef9e757f00f/scratchpad/muse-review-strong/build/tests/litmus.test.ts>). Environment note: `cd build && npm test` could not run in this checkout — `node_modules` is absent (`ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND: tsx`) and the sandbox has no network. All gate findings below were instead confirmed by executing the real [litmus.ts](</tmp/claude-1000/-home-james-projects-your-procedure-is-denied-build/9fc98b9d-e5c7-45fe-9c8e-9ef9e757f00f/scratchpad/muse-review-strong/build/src/litmus.ts>) module (copied to `/tmp`, imports rewired from `.js` to `.ts` only) under Node type-stripping, against the fixture chart from the gate's own tests. The repo was not modified (`git status` clean).

## Blocker

**B1. Dates written with a month name are not checked at all.** [sentenceHardTokens in litmus.ts:188](</tmp/claude-1000/-home-james-projects-your-procedure-is-denied-build/9fc98b9d-e5c7-45fe-9c8e-9ef9e757f00f/scratchpad/muse-review-strong/build/src/litmus.ts:188>) recognizes only ISO and slash dates; month names produce no token. Ran: citing `note-002` (dated 2025-08-14, quote the PT quote), both `The therapy note of September 14, 2025 documents completion.` and the December variant return `verified`. The existing test at [litmus.test.ts:197](</tmp/claude-1000/-home-james-projects-your-procedure-is-denied-build/9fc98b9d-e5c7-45fe-9c8e-9ef9e757f00f/scratchpad/muse-review-strong/build/tests/litmus.test.ts:197>) only exercises a wrong *day*, so this is untested. A model (or a judge in the viewer's gate editor) can move any appointment, surgery, or service date by months.

**B2. The number words "one", "zero", ordinals, and "dozen" are invisible to the gate.** [NUMBER_WORDS in litmus.ts:127](</tmp/claude-1000/-home-james-projects-your-procedure-is-denied-build/9fc98b9d-e5c7-45fe-9c8e-9ef9e757f00f/scratchpad/muse-review-strong/build/src/litmus.ts:127>) omits `one`/`zero`; ordinal forms (`fifteenth`) fail the `\b(...)\b` word boundary; `dozen` is unlisted. Ran, all `verified` against the test fixture: `The patient completed one week of physical therapy.` (entry: 12 weeks), `...zero weeks...`, `She was on one antianginal agent.` and `She was on a dozen antianginal agents.` (entry lists three drugs with no count — the exact "count the chart never states" case the README says is blocked, bypassed by wording), `She had XXIV months of upper back pain.` (Roman numerals also untokenized). The mutation harness mirrors the same word list ([mutate.ts:75](</tmp/claude-1000/-home-james-projects-your-procedure-is-denied-build/9fc98b9d-e5c7-45fe-9c8e-9ef9e757f00f/scratchpad/muse-review-strong/build/scripts/mutate.ts:75>)), so the spike-in cannot see this class either.

**B3. Anatomical side can be smuggled past the idiom mask or as an abbreviation.** [SIDE_IDIOM in litmus.ts:182](</tmp/claude-1000/-home-james-projects-your-procedure-is-denied-build/9fc98b9d-e5c7-45fe-9c8e-9ef9e757f00f/scratchpad/muse-review-strong/build/src/litmus.ts:182>) masks `right at`, `left in`, `right to`, etc. wherever they occur, and [the side extractor at litmus.ts:192](</tmp/claude-1000/-home-james-projects-your-procedure-is-denied-build/9fc98b9d-e5c7-45fe-9c8e-9ef9e757f00f/scratchpad/muse-review-strong/build/src/litmus.ts:192>) only matches the bare words `left|right`. Ran, all `verified` citing an entry with no side at all: `The lesion on the right at the chest wall persisted…`, `The RT knee pain persisted…`, `The R knee pain persisted…` — while the control `Her right shoulder pain…` correctly returned `needs-citation`. Laterality is the highest-harm token class in this domain (wrong-side surgery), and v1.4/v1.5 closed earlier side leaks while leaving this one.

**B4. The alphabetic part of a drug/procedure code is never compared.** [The code pattern at litmus.ts:191](</tmp/claude-1000/-home-james-projects-your-procedure-is-denied-build/9fc98b9d-e5c7-45fe-9c8e-9ef9e757f00f/scratchpad/muse-review-strong/build/src/litmus.ts:191>) (`\b[a-z]\d{2}…\b`) cannot match a 4-digit code like `J9271`, so only the digits are checked. Ran: against an entry reading `Start J9271 infusion today`, the sentences `She started K9271 infusion.` and `She started Q9271 infusion.` both return `verified`. J→K changes the drug entirely; the gate sees only `9271`.

## Serious

**S1. A sentence's content is never checked against its own quote, and evidence relevance is never checked — assembled, these pass a full packet.** [checkSentence in litmus.ts:298](</tmp/claude-1000/-home-james-projects-your-procedure-is-denied-build/9fc98b9d-e5c7-45fe-9c8e-9ef9e757f00f/scratchpad/muse-review-strong/build/src/litmus.ts:298>) checks only that the quote exists in the entry and that hard tokens exist *somewhere* admissible; the evidence loop ([litmus.ts:328](</tmp/claude-1000/-home-james-projects-your-procedure-is-denied-build/9fc98b9d-e5c7-45fe-9c8e-9ef9e757f00f/scratchpad/muse-review-strong/build/src/litmus.ts:328>)) verifies a quote's presence, not its bearing on the criterion, and [litmus.ts:343](</tmp/claude-1000/-home-james-projects-your-procedure-is-denied-build/9fc98b9d-e5c7-45fe-9c8e-9ef9e757f00f/scratchpad/muse-review-strong/build/src/litmus.ts:343>) marks a criterion verified on any verbatim quote. Ran: one packet combining B1+B2+B4+B3 fabrications plus `Blood pressure check` cited as evidence for the resection-weight criterion returned `verdict: pass`, all sentences `verified`. Separately, `She has metastatic breast cancer requiring urgent mastectomy and chemotherapy.` citing the quote `Still in the supportive bra` returned `verified` (fabricated diagnosis, no hard token). The README's Limitations ([README.md:426](</tmp/claude-1000/-home-james-projects-your-procedure-is-denied-build/9fc98b9d-e5c7-45fe-9c8e-9ef9e757f00f/scratchpad/muse-review-strong/README.md:426>)) discloses the sentence-vs-quote gap honestly, but the Abstract's "every sentence held to the record" and the Conclusion's "has not let a fabrication through in 5,824 tries" ([README.md:442](</tmp/claude-1000/-home-james-projects-your-procedure-is-denied-build/9fc98b9d-e5c7-45fe-9c8e-9ef9e757f00f/scratchpad/muse-review-strong/README.md:442>)) overstate what was measured.

**S2. Token provenance is pooled, so numbers can be recombined into fabricated quantities.** [sourceTokens in litmus.ts:201](</tmp/claude-1000/-home-james-projects-your-procedure-is-denied-build/9fc98b9d-e5c7-45fe-9c8e-9ef9e757f00f/scratchpad/muse-review-strong/build/src/litmus.ts:201>) splits every date into year/month/day components admitted as bare numbers. Ran, all `verified`: `She completed 14 weeks of physical therapy.` citing the entry dated 08-14 that says 12 weeks (14 comes from the date); `She completed 6 months of physical therapy…` (6 comes only from the criterion text); `The estimated resection was 2,200 grams…` (composed from `5 foot 2, 200 pounds` in the cited entry); `…690 grams on the right and 724 on the left…` (the entry assigns them the other way round — pairing is never checked). The collision class in Table 3 covers criteria/denial/facts reuse, but date components, thousands composition, and side↔number re-pairing are not among the 9,518 mutations.

**S3. Non-ASCII digits bypass number checking entirely.** JS `\d` is ASCII-only and [canon in litmus.ts:115](</tmp/claude-1000/-home-james-projects-your-procedure-is-denied-build/9fc98b9d-e5c7-45fe-9c8e-9ef9e757f00f/scratchpad/muse-review-strong/build/src/litmus.ts:115>) performs no digit folding. Ran: `The estimated resection was ９９９ grams.` (fullwidth digits) returns `verified` against an entry whose only weights are 724/690. Lower likelihood from a model than B1–B4, but it is a one-character-class fix (normalize Unicode decimal digits in `canon`).

**S4. A mid-loop provider failure silently zeroes cost, latency, usage, and the tool trace.** [proposeAgentic in provider.ts:183](</tmp/claude-1000/-home-james-projects-your-procedure-is-denied-build/9fc98b9d-e5c7-45fe-9c8e-9ef9e757f00f/scratchpad/muse-review-strong/build/src/provider.ts:183>) accumulates usage/trace locally and returns them only on success; any throw (rate limit on turn 5 of 24, say) propagates to [runCase in harness.ts:360](</tmp/claude-1000/-home-james-projects-your-procedure-is-denied-build/9fc98b9d-e5c7-45fe-9c8e-9ef9e757f00f/scratchpad/muse-review-strong/build/src/harness.ts:360>), which records `EMPTY_USAGE`, `costUsd: 0`, `latencyMs: 0`. Read-confirmed. Billable turns vanish from the run's cost accounting and the partial reading trace — the evidence a failure investigation needs most — is discarded. The same shape recurs in the repair path and in `advise.ts`.

**S5. `regate` re-gates only the final draft and leaves stale gate records inside the file it re-stamps.** [regate in regate.ts:47](</tmp/claude-1000/-home-james-projects-your-procedure-is-denied-build/9fc98b9d-e5c7-45fe-9c8e-9ef9e757f00f/scratchpad/muse-review-strong/build/scripts/regate.ts:47>) recomputes `gate` and `outcome` but not `firstGate`, `repairs[].gate`, `repairs[].outcome`, `firstOutcome`, `warrantedMatch`, or `citationPrecision` (the last derives from the evidence it just re-checked), and its `changedStatuses` counter ignores evidence-status changes. After a gate version bump, a repair file would declare the new version in its header while the viewer's repair replay ([replay.ts:408](</tmp/claude-1000/-home-james-projects-your-procedure-is-denied-build/9fc98b9d-e5c7-45fe-9c8e-9ef9e757f00f/scratchpad/muse-review-strong/build/viewer/src/replay.ts:408>)) renders old-version stamps for the first draft and repair turns. Latent in the committed files (repair runs postdate v1.5) but it defeats the tool's stated purpose on the next version bump. Read-confirmed; [regate.test.ts](</tmp/claude-1000/-home-james-projects-your-procedure-is-denied-build/9fc98b9d-e5c7-45fe-9c8e-9ef9e757f00f/scratchpad/muse-review-strong/build/tests/regate.test.ts>) has no repair-file case.

**S6. The harness CLI accepts inputs that produce a silent "successful" empty run.** [harness.ts:642](</tmp/claude-1000/-home-james-projects-your-procedure-is-denied-build/9fc98b9d-e5c7-45fe-9c8e-9ef9e757f00f/scratchpad/muse-review-strong/build/src/harness.ts:642>): a mistyped `--case case-999` filters to zero cases, and the run writes a results file with `cases: 0`, prints a summary, and exits 0. `--limit abc` does the same via `slice(0, NaN)`; `--concurrency abc` yields zero workers in [mapWithConcurrency at harness.ts:437](</tmp/claude-1000/-home-james-projects-your-procedure-is-denied-build/9fc98b9d-e5c7-45fe-9c8e-9ef9e757f00f/scratchpad/muse-review-strong/build/src/harness.ts:437>) and crashes opaquely inside `summarize`. `--repair` accepts any non-negative integer with no cap on turns or spend. Read-confirmed.

**S7. An unpriced model id throws after the billable call and discards a valid draft.** [costUsd in cost.ts:30](</tmp/claude-1000/-home-james-projects-your-procedure-is-denied-build/9fc98b9d-e5c7-45fe-9c8e-9ef9e757f00f/scratchpad/muse-review-strong/build/src/cost.ts:30>) throws on unknown price keys; it is called after `messages.create` succeeds in all three provider methods (e.g. [provider.ts:247](</tmp/claude-1000/-home-james-projects-your-procedure-is-denied-build/9fc98b9d-e5c7-45fe-9c8e-9ef9e757f00f/scratchpad/muse-review-strong/build/src/provider.ts:247>)), so `--provider meta --model <anything new>` turns every case into a cost-0 `error` with the paid-for draft thrown away. The documented Baseten/Fireworks paths are shielded by hardcoded price keys; the Meta path is not. Read-confirmed.

## Minor

- **OpenAI fallback weaknesses** ([provider.ts:323](</tmp/claude-1000/-home-james-projects-your-procedure-is-denied-build/9fc98b9d-e5c7-45fe-9c8e-9ef9e757f00f/scratchpad/muse-review-strong/build/src/provider.ts:323>), read): no fetch timeout (a hung Fireworks call stalls a concurrency worker and the whole run forever, unlike the 180 s Messages path), no `proposeAgentic` (so `--agentic --provider fireworks` errors all 50 cases into a results file instead of failing fast), and `prompt_tokens − cached_tokens` can go negative on an inconsistent usage block — [count in provider.ts:137](</tmp/claude-1000/-home-james-projects-your-procedure-is-denied-build/9fc98b9d-e5c7-45fe-9c8e-9ef9e757f00f/scratchpad/muse-review-strong/build/src/provider.ts:137>) rejects non-numbers but not negatives, so cost can be understated.
- **max-turns transcript is not resumable as documented.** When the agentic loop exhausts turns, [provider.ts:236](</tmp/claude-1000/-home-james-projects-your-procedure-is-denied-build/9fc98b9d-e5c7-45fe-9c8e-9ef9e757f00f/scratchpad/muse-review-strong/build/src/provider.ts:236>) leaves the transcript ending in an unanswered `tool_result` user turn while the interface promises "the whole exchange, for a repair turn." No current caller resumes a max-turns result, so this is latent.
- **Intake silently zeroes missing usage fields** ([intake.ts:107](</tmp/claude-1000/-home-james-projects-your-procedure-is-denied-build/9fc98b9d-e5c7-45fe-9c8e-9ef9e757f00f/scratchpad/muse-review-strong/build/src/intake.ts:107>)) where the main provider deliberately throws — an API usage-shape change would understate intake cost with no signal. Its `costUsd` call also sits outside the try block, so an unpriced `--model` crashes the whole intake run after paid calls.
- **Viewer gate editor stamps an empty sentence "verified."** Ran via the probe: `checkSentence` with `text: ''` (or `'.'`) and any valid quote returns `verified`. A judge who clears the sentence box in "test the gate" sees the gate bless nothing. Cosmetic for the stored verdict, confusing in a demo whose centerpiece is this control.
- **Viewer race on rapid run switching.** [selectFile in main.ts:762](</tmp/claude-1000/-home-james-projects-your-procedure-is-denied-build/9fc98b9d-e5c7-45fe-9c8e-9ef9e757f00f/scratchpad/muse-review-strong/build/viewer/src/main.ts:762>) has no sequencing token; two in-flight fetches resolve in network order, so quickly flipping the run picker can land on the earlier selection. Also: keydown playback shortcuts still fire while the footnote `<dialog>` is open if focus is not on a form control, and `renderCompare`/`renderBoard` fetch failures surface only as unhandled promise rejections.
- **Dictation echoes the transcript to stderr** ([dictation.ts:124](</tmp/claude-1000/-home-james-projects-your-procedure-is-denied-build/9fc98b9d-e5c7-45fe-9c8e-9ef9e757f00f/scratchpad/muse-review-strong/build/src/dictation.ts:124>)). Harmless for the synthetic TTS stand-in; if this pipeline is ever pointed at a real dictated note, the transcript lands in terminal logs by default.
- **Spec drift on quote normalization.** §2.4 says quotes match with "whitespace, case, and quote glyphs normalized and nothing else," but [canon in litmus.ts:115](</tmp/claude-1000/-home-james-projects-your-procedure-is-denied-build/9fc98b9d-e5c7-45fe-9c8e-9ef9e757f00f/scratchpad/muse-review-strong/build/src/litmus.ts:115>) also folds dash variants, NBSP, and NFC. The gate's own header comment discloses this; the manuscript and the MCP server's rules ([server.ts:19](</tmp/claude-1000/-home-james-projects-your-procedure-is-denied-build/9fc98b9d-e5c7-45fe-9c8e-9ef9e757f00f/scratchpad/muse-review-strong/build/litmus-gate/src/server.ts:19>)) do not. Ran: a quote with an em dash substituted for the entry's hyphen verifies.
- **Table 3's "caught" includes `needs-citation`** — 167 of 1,194 number-absent, all 225 laterality-swap, and all 43 idiom-leak catches are `needs-citation`, not `refuted` (verified from `report.json` byKind statuses). The table footnote does disclose "caught meaning refuted or needs-citation," and a blocked draft is operationally caught — but "hard corruption" prose elsewhere reads as refutation.
- **Advisor summary counts attempted cases as advised.** [summarizeAdvice in advise.ts:84](</tmp/claude-1000/-home-james-projects-your-procedure-is-denied-build/9fc98b9d-e5c7-45fe-9c8e-9ef9e757f00f/scratchpad/muse-review-strong/build/scripts/advise.ts:84>) includes the 2 cases whose answers were not valid JSON in "91 drafted cases," though they contributed no criteria judgments. The numbers still reconcile (363 criteria are the judged ones); the wording is slightly generous.

## Nit

- [litmus.test.ts:203](</tmp/claude-1000/-home-james-projects-your-procedure-is-denied-build/9fc98b9d-e5c7-45fe-9c8e-9ef9e757f00f/scratchpad/muse-review-strong/build/tests/litmus.test.ts:203>) still titles a test "laterality is a hard token in anatomical context only" — the v1.3 behavior v1.4 deliberately replaced. The assertions pass; the title now teaches the wrong rule.
- §3's "A modifier denial (CARC 4) was declined without opening a single entry" is true of 3 of the 6 agentic runs (verified from traces); in the three live-CHART runs the models read 5 entries first. Existentially true, easy to misread as the behavior.
- The viewer loads Google Fonts ([index.html:9](</tmp/claude-1000/-home-james-projects-your-procedure-is-denied-build/9fc98b9d-e5c7-45fe-9c8e-9ef9e757f00f/scratchpad/muse-review-strong/build/viewer/index.html:9>)) — the only third-party request on a page judges may open on a conference network; it degrades gracefully offline.

## What I found clean

- **The verbatim-quote core.** Ran: a one-word-changed quote, a real quote on the wrong entry, an empty quote, and a trivial quote are all refuted; unknown/malformed citations are `unresolved`, never passes; a throwing check becomes `error` and blocks. The [brand-symbol design in litmus.ts:64](</tmp/claude-1000/-home-james-projects-your-procedure-is-denied-build/9fc98b9d-e5c7-45fe-9c8e-9ef9e757f00f/scratchpad/muse-review-strong/build/src/litmus.ts:64>) genuinely prevents other modules from minting `verified` at the type level, and compound/hundred number words (the live-found v1.1/v1.2 defects) read correctly in both directions.
- **The manuscript's numbers.** I recomputed from the result files: all 9 kept-run agreement/false-pass/cost/latency/defended figures in Table 1; repeat ranges in Table 2 (including the two-model-id Spark Open pool, disclosed in prose); payer, repair (6 of 7 blocked drafts repaired, 0 false passes created), effort, and intake tables (46/50 letters, the same 4 KDOB1→KD0B1 glyph errors named); mutation totals (5,824 hard / 1,308 collision / 2,386 soft = 9,518, `report.json` at gate v1.5 with 0 hard passes); advisor aggregates (91 cases, 363 criteria, $2.47, the case-023 partial on exactly the intensity criterion); 30/20 warranted split, $940,000/$568,500 stakes, 19–35 entries (mean 25.6), 18 distinct services, ~64% distractor entries; and the 263 test count (matches a static count of `test(` definitions exactly). Every kept file carries its `regated` chain with `changedVerdicts: 0` at each step, as claimed. Fabrication prose is precise: the 2 evidence-item fabrications are on model-declined drafts, and no kept/repeat *sentence* carries a fabricated quote.
- **Viewer robustness across the data.** Ran `buildTimeline`/`stateAt` from [replay.ts](</tmp/claude-1000/-home-james-projects-your-procedure-is-denied-build/9fc98b9d-e5c7-45fe-9c8e-9ef9e757f00f/scratchpad/muse-review-strong/build/viewer/src/replay.ts>) over all 19 viewer-listed files × 950 results × 19,624 steps: no throws, end-state verdicts and verified counts match the stored gate records everywhere, and malformed step/case inputs clamp or fall back. All rendering goes through `textContent`/`createElement` — I found no `innerHTML` or equivalent anywhere in the viewer, so stored draft text cannot inject markup. Editor citations come from a `<select>` of real entry ids, so the in-browser recheck cannot be crashed from the UI.
- **Security and data.** No secrets anywhere in the tree (keys are read from gitignored `.env` and named only in error messages); error paths deliberately strip SDK messages and model text down to exception class and HTTP status ([harness.ts:361](</tmp/claude-1000/-home-james-projects-your-procedure-is-denied-build/9fc98b9d-e5c7-45fe-9c8e-9ef9e757f00f/scratchpad/muse-review-strong/build/src/harness.ts:361>), [schema.ts:87](</tmp/claude-1000/-home-james-projects-your-procedure-is-denied-build/9fc98b9d-e5c7-45fe-9c8e-9ef9e757f00f/scratchpad/muse-review-strong/build/src/schema.ts:87>)). All patient-like content is `SYN-###` aliases with age/sex against six fictional payers; no names, SSNs, MRNs, or claim numbers exist in the synthetic set or results. The CHART tool validates code/date formats before fetching and sends no patient data ([chart.ts:138](</tmp/claude-1000/-home-james-projects-your-procedure-is-denied-build/9fc98b9d-e5c7-45fe-9c8e-9ef9e757f00f/scratchpad/muse-review-strong/build/src/chart.ts:138>)); stored drafts/`rawPreview` exist only because the corpus is synthetic, and the code says so at each site.

event.advisory_text: Exercise this the way the user will and judge it by the REAL result they'd get — the actual output a person experiences — not a proxy that can pass while it's broken (a syntax check, an HTTP 200, a DOM query, or a screenshot saved but never opened). When the real result is something only the eye can confirm — a rendered page, game, or UI — look at the render itself with a HEADLESS browser in the background (never a visible window that steals focus), not an inference from the DOM or logs. Scale the check to what this is — finish the WHOLE check in one pass, then stop once it's genuinely working rather than re-verifying — and fix and rerun anything that's off, without re-stating what was built until it's actually verified. Do that now with a tool.
